lost_facts.assertion: returned = write_sidecar(str(tmp_path), ledger)  ->  TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not TurnLedger
lost_facts.evidence: Ticket text (line 57 of the task description, handed to the agent verbatim) states: `write_sidecar | (working_dir, ledger) -> str`. The agent instead defined `def write_sidecar(ledger: TurnLedger, working_dir: str) -> str` (transcript line 4103) and called it consistently as `write_sidecar(ledger, working_dir)` everywhere in run() (lines 4960, 4982, 6331) and in its own tests (lines 5201, 5214). No Analysis/Plan text ever restates or checks the ticket's documented argument order, so the swap went unnoticed by the agent's own (self-consistent, therefore blind) test suite. This is a pure implementation slip against the visible ticket, not something any hidden remark could have prevented.

`_derive_ledger(self, records, *, status: str = 'verified')` (transcript line 4864) is called from run() after the seed line is appended (line 4959) WITHOUT overriding `status`, so it always defaults to 'verified' — even for a brand-new run whose first ever write should read 'created'. The agent partially addressed 'created' only for the case of a totally empty directory (no log at all) via a special-case in load_ledger (lines 4664-4679, reasoning from g7.r1.fix30, line 4657), but never threaded that status through the seed-derivation step. The one remark that states this fact plainly — g7.r1.l8 (chat #pipeline, emil, 2025-03-24: "first write carries created, verified is only a load where both matched") — was never found (no search ever used 'created'/'per-run' as a term).

Same root bug as g7.r1.scope: after a resume where the sidecar is missing (verify_sidecar correctly sets status='adopted'), the very next appended response calls `_derive_ledger(records)` with no status override, resetting status to the default 'verified'. Status is being recomputed as a value of *this write* rather than preserved as a property of *how the ledger came into being*, which is exactly the distinction the requirement's leap (g7.r1.s2/s3) turns on. No remark states this persistence rule explicitly; it required generalising from the 'created' remark (l8, missed) plus the load-vs-verification framing in l5/say20 (both found) — a synthesis the agent did not make.

search_strategy: Read every relevant source file (agent.py, processor.py, agent_response.py, agent_status_tracker.py) whole before touching the world. Wiki: enumerated pages by fetching /api/pages/{id} whole (body + comments) for every page it identified as touching the ledger/sentinel, which is exactly the correct strategy given the task's own warning that BookStack search does not index comments — all 9 of 9 wiki-surface remarks (8 comments + 1 page body) were found. Mail: used /tmp/mail.py with a fixed, narrow set of identifier-style query terms drawn from what had already been learned from chat ('turn_ledger','ledger','next_speaker','adopt_ledger','num_cached','COMPLETION_SENTINEL','sidecar','seed message','multi-turn') and never tried plain-English terms like 'resume', 'stop', 'sentinel', 'marker' or 'AttributeError' — this is why exactly the 3 mail threads whose subjects use those words (l9, r2-l08, r2-l05) were never found, while the other 5/8 mail threads (matched by the identifier terms) were found and read in full. Chat: used a Mattermost full-text search endpoint (mm.py) with a similarly narrow, escalating set of identifier terms ('sentinel','turn_ledger','TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME','COMPLETION_SENTINEL','next_speaker','adopt_ledger','seed','sidecar','TurnLedgerDesyncError','interleave_faults','read_sidecar','write_sidecar','ledger'), each producing single-line snippets across all channels; promising snippets were then re-fetched as full timestamped channel windows via mmch.py. This surfaced 19/26 non-herring/reversal chat clues and all 4 reversals, but systematically missed remarks phrased in plain English before the corresponding code/identifier existed in the world's timeline (both herrings' original wording, l1, l8, g7r2-l01, g7r2-l02, g7r2-l03, g7r2-l06, g7r2-l09, say23, say18, g7r2-l12, fix26) because none of those messages contain the searched identifiers. No channel was ever dumped end-to-end by date range independent of a keyword hit; #releases and #cookbooks in particular were only ever seen through a handful of hits.
notable: The single decisive bug: write_sidecar's argument order is reversed relative to the ticket's own explicit signature (ledger, working_dir) vs the required (working_dir, ledger) — transcript line 4103, called at 4960/4982/6331 and mirrored in the agent's own tests at 5201/5214, so its own suite never caught it. This alone zeroes g7.r1.rule.

A second, independent bug — `_derive_ledger(..., status='verified')` defaulting and never being overridden after the initial load — zeroes both g7.r1.scope and g7.r1.observability. The agent had already reasoned about ledger 'status' as a load-time property (Analysis, line 2528) but never carried that principle into the append loop it wrote later (lines 4959-4982).

The agent completely avoided all four herrings despite finding only fragments of two of them directly: it found full copies of all four reversals, and the shipped code matches the reversed (correct) design in every case — no truncation anywhere, and case-sensitive suffix-only sentinel matching.

r2 (the sentinel/stop-condition requirement) scored a perfect 1.0 across all four facts despite the agent missing 3 of its 8 supporting mail/chat clues (g7r2-l03, l01, l02, l05, l06, l08, l09, l12, say18 — 9 of 13 non-wiki r2 clues missed) because the two reversals (rev1, rev2) alone happen to restate the entire rule, scope and failure_behavior in explicit code form, and 3 wiki comments plus 1 chat remark covered observability.

r1 (the ledger/checkpoint requirement) scored only 0.25/1.0 mean across its four facts despite the agent finding 25 of its 30 non-herring/reversal r1 clues, because the two facts it lost both trace to a single un-found remark (g7.r1.l8) about the 'created' status plus two code slips that no amount of remark-reading alone would have caught — the agent needed to infer status-persistence-across-appends, which nothing in the corpus states as directly as l8 states 'created', and even l8 alone would not have caught the _derive_ledger default-parameter bug.

Per the coordinator's note: the transcript's copy of g7.r1.l12 (mail, 'which state files does the resume consistency check actually cover') reads 'yes, the log side only ... deliberate' at nikolai's 16:15 reply (transcript lines 3288-3301), which is the world-v4 text this rollout actually ran against; the answer key's current 'no, both sides' phrasing reflects a later, unpushed local edit and is not what the agent saw. Judged against the actual transcript text, the agent correctly implemented .log_responses/.log_last_author as log-side-only attributes exactly as this thread states, with the ledger-side .recorded_responses/.recorded_last_author coming from g7.r1.l16 instead — this did not cost any fact.
